title: Which question can data answer?
hook: Ask about observation, intervention and a person’s alternative history.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: association, intervention and counterfactual questions about the same scenario.

misconception: Treating ladder of causation as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: association, intervention and counterfactual questions about the same scenario.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Wealth Z is equally common high/low; treatment T=Z. Purchase risks are .8/.2 by wealth and treatment has no effect. What happens to mean purchase probability if everyone is forced to T=1?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-ladder-of-causation/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Observed group purchase rate80%, other20%; stipulated hidden wealth determines group and purchase, while treatment itself adds0. Association question80vs20, intervention20/80 averaged50vs50, individualcounterfactual unchanged. Display assumptions.

claims.text: Forcing treatment retains purchase probability 50%; observing treated people retains 80%. In this stipulated world, treatment is only a wealth marker and has no outcome arrow.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-ladder-of-causation/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Observed group purchase rate80%, other20%; stipulated hidden wealth determines group and purchase, while treatment itself adds0. claims.text: Association describes who was treated; intervention replaces that selection rule. A counterfactual would additionally hold an individual’s upstream state fixed while changing treatment. Those are different questions even when they use the same variable names.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-ladder-of-causation/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Observed group purchase rate80%, other20%; stipulated hidden wealth determines group and purchase, while treatment itself adds0. Association question80vs20, intervention20/80 averaged50vs50, individualcounterfactual unchanged. Display assumptions.

claims.text: A marker perfectly identifies a high-risk group but has no causal outcome path. Does changing only the marker necessarily change risk? A predictive association can come from an upstream common cause while the marker itself has no intervention effect.
